subject: Dedicated cluster footprint — seeding, baseline & phased ignite plan
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@crestline.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for Phase 1 production

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — really useful. We are finalizing our production plan for the clinical-NLP inference pipeline and need a clear set of dedicated capacity options to take to procurement. Key asks: cluster footprint options, minimum GPU commitment (what you call min-GPUs), a realistic ramp schedule (weeks to scale), and any warmup/burst windows you recommend.

Our initial traffic projections (attached in the doc I shared) show a steep ramp once model is in the wild — we want to avoid outages during rollout but also keep cost predictable. Can you send a short set of scenarios (low/mid/high) and call out recommended monitoring gates that trigger scale ups?

Procurement would like this by next week (they requested a written proposal). Also include any standard pre-warm credits or activation fees.

Appreciate it — Alice
Director of ML Engineering
Crestline Therapeutics
Attachment: traffic-profiles-phase1.xlsx (referenced)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@crestline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for Phase 1 production

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear brief and the traffic file. Attached is a concise pack with three scenarios and a proposed ramp cadence (crestline_dedicated_options_v1.pdf). Summary below so procurement can pick a path quickly: 

Scenario A — Seed (cost-conscious, fast start):
- Initial cluster: 12x A40-equivalent GPUs (single-AZ)
- Min-GPU lock: 8 GPUs (keeps a small baseline for cold starts)
- Ramp: Maintain seed for 4–6 weeks while validating throughput and error budget; scale to Baseline if p95 latency <350ms and token throughput >120k/day for 3 consecutive days.
- Warmup: 40k warmup credits included (one-time)

Scenario B — Baseline (recommended for production reliability):
- Initial cluster: 24x A40-equivalent GPUs (multi-AZ active-passive routing)
- Min-GPU lock: 20 GPUs (keeps steady-state headroom for KV cache growth)
- Ramp: Seed -> Baseline by week 6; policy-driven autoscale window for short bursts; target p99 <450ms.

Scenario C — Anchor (throughput-first, long horizon):
- Initial cluster: 48x A40-equivalent GPUs (multi-AZ, reserved lanes)
- Min-GPU lock: 40 GPUs
- Ramp: Phase to Anchor over 12 weeks only after agreed milestone (30% sustained growth). Includes burst credits and canaries.

Decision cadence / gating suggestions:
- Week 0: Go-live in Seed (12 GPUs) with synthetic load tests and 24/7 on-call for first 72 hours.
- Gate 1 (Wk 4–6): Promote to Baseline if throughput + latency KPIs met.
- Gate 2 (Wk 8–12): Promote to Anchor if utilization >70% and product KPIs show positive regression.

I attached a mutual action plan (MAP_Crestline_2026.xlsx) with suggested dates and acceptance criteria. If procurement wants a narrower min-GPU to save cost, we can propose a 16 GPU min floor but we’ll need a slightly larger warmup credit to avoid cold-tail latency.

Next steps: happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement next Tue/Wed. If you confirm which scenario you prefer, I’ll draft the SOW line items and activation calendar.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment: crestline_dedicated_options_v1.pdf, MAP_Crestline_2026.xlsx

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster footprint — internal sizing notes

Matt/Team — quick internal notes after reviewing Mateo's scenarios. Keeping this short: 

1) Min-GPU recommendation tweak: 20 (instead of 24) for Baseline makes sense to reduce TCO and still meet 95% of expected loads; call out the risk window (first 2 weeks) where p99 can spike. Recommend adding a 48–72 hour accelerated warmup (prefetch prefix caching) on cutover to avoid cold KV misses.

2) Autoscale behavior: recommend a conservative immediate burst allowance (+20%) for 30 minutes, then scale-back policies to avoid oscillation. Put a 10-minute cooldown.

3) SLA & credits: include one free canary activation (2 hours) and two 4-hour warmup credits in the SOW. Procurement will like explicit line items.

4) Cost guardrail: propose a soft cap alert when expected daily token spend increases >15% vs projected to trigger outbound sales/cost review.

If procurement pushes for lower min-GPUs, we should present a variant with a slightly higher hourly burst price to compensate.

I can draft SOW language for the warmup/credits and the autoscale rules if Mateo wants.

— Chloe
Sr Solutions Engineer

From: Alice Park <alice@crestline.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@crestline.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster footprint — seeding, baseline & phased ignite plan

Thanks Mateo / team — this is helpful. Procurement passed along a short checklist (attached) and asked for two clarifications before we move to SOW: 

1) What exactly does ‘min-GPU lock’ mean for billing? Is procurement billed for the full min-GPU floor even if we use less during a given billing period?
2) How are ramp triggers enforced operationally? We need the concrete conditions you’ll use to authorize a scale — e.g., whether it’s automated by telemetry or manual approval.

We like Scenario B (Baseline) as our target path but are open to starting at Scenario A if it reduces immediate spend. Please include SOW line items and the activation calendar; procurement asked whether there are any termination or step-down notice windows tied to a reserved fleet. 

Attachment: procurement_checklist.pdf

Best,
Alice

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@crestline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster footprint — seeding, baseline & phased ignite plan (SOW draft + clarifications)

Alice — good questions. Short answers up front then the formal SOW attachment.

1) Billing for min-GPU lock: The min-GPU floor is billed as reserved capacity for the billing period you select. If you commit to a min 20 GPUs, procurement is billed on that reservation basis (monthly pro-rata) even if utilization is lower. We model 30% effective utilization in our pricing examples to be conservative. Separately, burst usage above min is billed on top at metered rates and will appear on the same invoice.

2) Ramp triggers / enforcement: We support two modes: automatic (policy-driven) and manual (procurement/product approval). For Crestline we recommend a hybrid approach: automated telemetry triggers when throughput/latency gates are met (example: p95 <350ms, sustained throughput >120k/day for 72h), but any promotion that changes reserved min-GPU floor or billing commitment requires a documented approval (email chain or HubSpot deal stage change). Operationally we will open a change ticket in our activation tracker and run a canary every promotion to validate model correctness.

3) Termination / step-down: We offer a 60-day step-down window for reserved lanes (standard in SOW). Early decommitment carries a shortfall calculation; we'll include examples in the SOW so procurement can see potential exposures.

Proposed activation calendar (draft SOW lines):
- Go-live seed: 2026-11-15 -> Seed cluster 12 GPUs active (single AZ).
- Baseline promotion: by 2026-12-20 -> 24 GPUs active (min lock 20 GPUs).
- Anchor promotion (optional): by 2027-02-01 -> 48 GPUs active (min lock 40 GPUs).

Included in SOW draft: 2 warmup credits (4 hours each), 1 canary activation (2 hours), explicit autoscale policy, and a step-down/60-day termination clause. I attached SOW_Crestline_Dedicated_20261006.docx and linked the HubSpot deal (HS-CRS-312). If this looks OK, can you ask procurement for signature or an email approval on the MAP by 2026-10-14 so we can reserve capacity lead-time for Nov 15?

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if procurement wants a walkthrough.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_Crestline_Dedicated_20261006.docx
Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-CRS-312
